articles.summary: Actor Pamela Anderson joined a star-studded fundraising dinner in New York City that raised more than $5 million for organisations working to end
articles.body: Actor Pamela Anderson joined a star-studded fundraising dinner in New York City that raised more than $5 million for organisations working to end gender-based violence. The fifth annual Caring for Women Dinner, organised by the Kering Foundation, took place on September 10, 2026, at The Pool restaurant in Manhattan during New York Fashion Week. Co-hosted by Salma Hayek Pinault and François-Henri Pinault, the event brought together celebrities, athletes, artists and philanthropists to support women and children affected by violence. This year's fundraising brought the initiative's five-year total to more than $20 million. The proceeds will benefit four non-profit organisations working across prevention, advocacy and survivor support, continuing the event's focus on funding services and initiatives addressing gender-based violence.Pamela Anderson joins celebrities at the Caring for Women DinnerAnderson was among the public figures associated with the fifth annual dinner, alongside gymnast Simone Biles, actors Dakota Johnson and Benicio Del Toro, polo player Nacho Figueras and artist Lorna Simpson. The gathering took place at The Pool, a restaurant in Manhattan's Seagram Building, and combined a formal dinner with speeches, fundraising auctions and entertainment.Actor Colman Domingo served as the evening's emcee, while auctioneer Lydia Fenet led the live bidding. The programme included a three-course dinner, films highlighting the work of the beneficiary organisations and a performance by singer Rita Ora. Paris Hilton DJed at the after-party.The event brought together figures from fashion, entertainment, sport, art and philanthropy to support organisations working with survivors and communities affected by gender-based violence.Four organisations set to benefit from the fundsThe money raised at the 2026 dinner will support four organisations: Activating Change, Fondo Semillas, JBWS and The New York Women's Foundation. Each works in a different area of prevention, advocacy or support for people affected by gender-based violence.Activating Change works to advance disability justice and address violence against people with disabilities, including people who are deaf. Its work includes improving access to justice and services for survivors.Fondo Semillas is a Mexican feminist philanthropic organisation that supports grassroots groups working to advance women's rights, gender equality and bodily autonomy.JBWS, based in New Jersey, provides services for people affected by domestic violence. Its work includes crisis intervention, shelter and support for survivors seeking safety.The New York Women's Foundation funds community-led initiatives addressing gender, racial and economic inequalities. Its grantmaking supports organisations working to improve the safety, rights and opportunities of women and girls.The Kering Foundation has not announced how the total will be divided among the four beneficiaries. The organisations represent different parts of the response to gender-based violence, from direct support for survivors to prevention and broader social change.How the dinner raised more than $5 millionFundraising included contributions from guests and supporters, a live auction and an online silent auction that was opened to the public for the first time. The live auction featured artwork, luxury products and exclusive experiences contributed by supporters.Among the reported results, three collages by artist Lorna Simpson sold for $165,000, while an experience at Dataland, a planned museum of AI-generated art, fetched $45,000. A palmetto diamond necklace sold for $130,000.The online auction ran from September 1 to September 14, allowing people beyond the dinner's attendees to participate. Items included a signed leotard worn by Biles during her winning performance at the 2021 US Classic, a limited-edition Gucci handbag and fashion-related experiences.Salma Hayek Pinault and François-Henri Pinault's roleSalma Hayek Pinault and her husband, François-Henri Pinault, have served as the dinner's founding co-hosts since its launch in 2022. Pinault is chairman of Kering, the luxury group, and the Kering Foundation.The initiative was created to mobilise support for organisations working to end violence against women and children. The annual gathering seeks to turn that commitment into financial support for organisations working directly with affected communities.Established in 2008, the Kering Foundation supports programmes intended to prevent violence, help survivors and promote safer environments for women and children. Its work extends across several countries and includes partnerships with non-profit organisations, service providers and advocacy groups.Five years of fundraising for survivorsSince its first edition in 2022, the Caring for Women Dinner has raised more than $20 million across five years, according to the Kering Foundation. The 2026 total followed the more than $4.5 million raised at the 2025 dinner.The foundation's wider partnerships support work ranging from legal information and assistance for survivors to crisis services, prevention programmes and educational opportunities. It has reported reaching more than three million women and children through its broader work over nearly two decades.The scale of the issue remains substantial. The World Health Organization estimates that approximately one in three women worldwide experience physical and/or sexual violence during their lifetime. The figure underscores the need for prevention, survivor services and long-term support beyond individual fundraising events.The fifth dinner brought together public figures and organisations around that shared goal, with this year's proceeds directed to four non-profits working on different aspects of the response to gender-based violence.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2018, Simon Cowell donated £25,000 to help close a South Korean dog meat farm; the charity’s rescue operation moved more than 200 dogs and puppies towards shelter care and a chance of adoption
articles.summary: British television personality and music producer Simon Cowell donated £25,000 to help an animal welfare charity close a dog meat farm in South Korea.
articles.body: British television personality and music producer Simon Cowell donated £25,000 to help an animal welfare charity close a dog meat farm in South Korea. The donation which happened in the year 2018, supported a rescue operation by Humane Society International (HSI), which was working to save more than 200 dogs and puppies kept at the farm for the meat trade.According to HSI, the animals had spent their lives inside small metal cages, with little space to move and limited human contact. Some were suffering from untreated injuries and skin conditions. The charity planned to remove them from the farm and transfer them to shelters in other countries, where they could receive care and eventually be considered for adoption.The rescue was part of HSI's wider campaign to end dog meat farming in South Korea. By September 2018, the organisation had already closed 12 farms and rescued nearly 1,400 dogs. Cowell's contribution helped support its next operation, which became the charity's 13th farm closure in the country.The dogs were then transportation to the United States, United Kingdom, the Netherlands and Canada. Among the animals were around 90 puppies born in the preceding weeks.Simon Cowell on dog meat tradeCowell's involvement with the rescue was not his first contribution to HSI's campaign. In 2017, he had spoken about the treatment of dogs on meat farms during an interview with Good Morning Britain, shortly before another HSI rescue mission to South Korea. He had said, "It's like eating your friend. It's the fact you're eating such a kind, helpless, sweet animal."His £25,000 donation the following year came as the charity was preparing to close another farm. At the time, HSI said the money would provide an important boost to its rescue appeal.Claire Bass, then executive director of HSI UK, welcomed the contribution and explained why the organisation was trying to help farmers leave the dog meat business."Simon’s generous donation means the world to us, and provides a huge boost to our appeal to close this horrendous dog meat farm," she said.Inside the South Korean farmThe farm had been operating for 14 years before its owner approached HSI for help in leaving the industry. With the charity's assistance, the farmer planned to switch to growing medicinal herbs.According to Kitty Block, president of Humane Society International (HSI) in 2018, the animals were kept in bare cages with iron bars forming the floors. These bars caused discomfort to their paws, particularly during South Korea's cold winters.The rescue team found several breeds, including golden retrievers, Labrador retrievers, Tibetan mastiffs, Korean jindos and a Great Dane mix. Some dogs had untreated medical problems, while others were severely underweight.One Belgian Malinois, named Jean Claude by the rescuers, was particularly weak when the team first encountered him. Adam Parascandola, HSI's senior director of animal protection, opened his cage, and the dog came out and rested his head on Parascandola's lap."It was heartbreaking to see that of all that was missing in his life- food, exercise, enrichment. What he wanted most is just the touch of a person," Parascandola said.Another dog, a shar-pei named Quentin, was almost blind because of an untreated eye infection.Dogs prepared for shelter careFollowing the farm's closure, HSI began arrangements to move the dogs overseas. The rescue operation included nearly 200 dogs and puppies, with destinations across North America and Europe.The charity had initially expected most animals to travel to Canada, while a smaller number would be taken to the UK. Its subsequent update also identified the United States and the Netherlands as destinations. The animals were to be placed in shelters before being considered for adoption.As the rescue team began caring for the animals, staff provided dry dog food and treats. Block reported that the dogs were becoming more responsive to their carers, greeting them with barking, wagging tails and physical affection.South Korea's dog meat industry faces oppositionAt the time of the rescue, HSI estimated that approximately 2.5 million dogs were being raised annually for meat on thousands of farms across South Korea.However, the charity reported that dog meat consumption was declining, particularly among younger South Koreans. Public opposition was also increasing.In July 2018, a petition calling for an end to the trade attracted more than 200,000 signatures on the South Korean government's website, prompting an official response from the president's office.The government indicated that it would consider removing dogs from the legal definition of livestock. Meanwhile, legal decisions and planned slaughterhouse closures were adding pressure on the industry.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US Department of Energy declares Power Grid Emergency in 13 States: What it is, and what it means for the residents of the states impacted
articles.summary: US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has issued an emergency order authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the
articles.body: US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright has issued an emergency order authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions, to run designated power generation units as needed to protect grid stability. The federal directive, issued on October 12, grants PJM temporary emergency authority running from October 13 through October 16. Under the order, the grid operator can mandate certain power plants to generate electricity and, in limited circumstances, tap into backup power reserves to maintain a steady flow of energy across its multistate network, as per the order available on the department’s official website. Federal officials and grid managers clarified that the order is designed specifically to prevent power interruptions and not to announce scheduled blackouts.Why the emergency order has been issuedHeadquartered in the Philadelphia area, PJM Interconnection coordinates wholesale electricity movement across all or parts of 13 states and the District of Columbia.“PJM serves as the Reliability Coordinator and Balancing Authority for its region and is, therefore, responsible for overseeing the dispatch of generation to meet system demand at all times within the limits of the transmission system. The PJM Region includes all or parts of Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia,” the order says.Ahead of strained conditions, the operator issued a Maximum Generation Alert and a Load Management Alert for October 13, pointing to a confluence of weather and scheduled infrastructure downtime. Due to ‘unseasonably warm autumn weather’, forecasted electricity demand is expected to reach approximately 111,500 megawatts or higher on October 13.The second reason is the maintenance window. The grid is currently in its standard seasonal outage cycle, which runs from mid-September through early December. During this period, utilities routinely take generation units and power lines offline for maintenance and upgrades to ensure peak availability ahead of freezing winter weather.Scheduled transmission line outages have restricted the volume of electricity that can be transferred between different zones on the system.According to the Department of Energy (DOE), without emergency federal intervention, PJM faced conditions where it might have had to reduce or cut power service to keep the regional grid balanced."It is our understanding that PJM seeks to unlock and deploy backup generation resources (whether auxiliary, standby, directly-connected, battery storage, or other, and whether synchronized or not to the bulk-power system) at data centers (including, but not limited to, hyperscaler facilities) and at other large load industrial and commercial customer sites as another tool to mitigate any undue risk to the bulk-power system," the order noted.What it means for residents in impacted US statesWhile PJM emphasised that the initial alert does not require immediate mandatory action from household customers, the operational strain could bring voluntary conservation measures into play. Day-to-day electricity usage remains normal, and the emergency declaration is aimed at coordinating power plants to keep systems stable.PJM has, however, issued capacity advisories and has the option to activate demand response initiatives. If conditions tighten, businesses and residents across the 13-state footprint could be asked to voluntarily dial back non-essential power consumption during peak hours.NERC Reliability Standard EOP-011-4 addresses Emergency Operations. Requirement 2 provides that “[e]ach Balancing Authority shall develop, maintain, and implement one or more Reliability Coordinator-reviewed Operating Plan(s) to mitigate Capacity Emergencies and Energy Emergencies within its Balancing Authority Area.”Balancing Authorities are responsible for requesting that their respective Reliability Coordinators issue an EEA in accordance with Requirement 2 and Attachment 1 to Reliability Standard EOP-011-4. Among other things, Requirement 2.2.4 of this reliability standard authorizes Balancing Authorities to make “[p]ublic appeals for voluntary Load reductions.”Moreover, section 2.2.9 requires Balancing Authority Operating plans to include provisions for “Transmission Operators to implement operator-controlled manual Load shedding, undervoltage Load shedding, or underfrequency Load shedding,” and section 2.2.10 requires such plans to determine reliability impacts of “extreme weather conditions.”These procedures align with North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Reliability Standard EOP-011-4, which governs emergency operations. Under these standards, balancing authorities must maintain plans to handle capacity shortfalls and extreme weather impacts.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Young Londoners invited to name two beaves born in Ealing
articles.summary: Londoners aged four to 18 can suggest names for the kits, born at Paradise Fields, until 7 December.
articles.body:
Children in London are being asked to help name two baby beavers born this year in west London.

Anyone living in the capital aged between four and 18 can suggest names for the kits until 7 December.

The winners will be chosen by representatives of the Ealing Beaver Project and the mayor of London's office.

A family of Eurasian beavers was released at Paradise Fields in Greenford in 2023, returning the animals to urban London for the first time in more than 400 years.

Elliot Newton, director of rewilding at conservation group Citizen Zoo, said the new kits showed beavers could "coexist with people in the heart of urban London".

The project's lead, Dr Sean McCormack, said: "Personally, I'm very excited to see what names the children come up with."

The scheme is run by Citizen Zoo, Ealing Wildlife Group, Friends of Horsenden Hill and Ealing Council, with funding from the mayor's office.

Its backers say the beavers have created new wetland habitats on the site, improved water quality and made the area more resilient to flooding and drought.

Paradise Fields is free to visit and open 24 hours a day.

Entries can be submitted through Citizen Zoo's website.

articles.title: Trial in college student’s murder zeroes in on rum bottle, vulgar note and missing evidence
articles.summary: Miguel Enrique Salguero-Olivares faces murder, rape and burglary charges in the Faith Hedgepeth case as DNA and missing evidence clash in court.
articles.body: Fourteen years after authorities found Faith Hedgepeth dead, the 19-year-old’s final hours have been unfolding in a North Carolina courtroom, where tearful testimony and questions about missing evidence marked the opening days of a murder trial. Miguel Enrique Salguero-Olivares, 33, is on trial in Durham County Superior Court on charges of first-degree murder, rape, sexual offense and burglary in the 2012 killing of Hedgepeth, a biology major at the University of North Carolina-Chapel Hill. Family members of Hedgepeth said they did not know her alleged killer and the two had no known prior interactions. The trial is in its second week, with Dr. Heather Waleski, a sexual assault nurse examiner with Atrium Health, testifying about forensic medical evidence. The first days of testimony brought tears from witnesses, spectators and jurors, the 9th Street Journal reported. A forensic technician showed the murder weapon to the jury. Close-up photographs of Hedgepeth’s face and body prompted some court spectators to cover their faces. SLAIN UNC STUDENT’S MOTHER HOPES NEW DOCUMENTARY WILL SHED LIGHT ON UNSOLVED MURDER: ‘I NEED TO KEEP GOING FOR HER’ The graphic descriptions of internal brain trauma overwhelmed the jury box, prompting the judge to call a recess Friday. Prosecutors and defense attorneys have clashed over whether DNA evidence revealed the killer or an unreliable investigation where key physical evidence vanished. A roommate's discovery Hedgepeth's roommate, Karena Rosario, now 34, sobbed Wednesday as she recalled finding Hedgepeth nude from the waist down in their shared bedroom at a nearby off-campus apartment, off Old Chapel Hill Road. "I walked around the bed and saw hair. I pulled the comforter down and saw she had a black eye," Rosario said, ABC 11 reported. Rosario took jurors back to Sept. 6, 2012, when she and Hedgepeth studied at a campus library before returning to their apartment to change. The pair then walked to The Thrill nightclub. MURDER SUSPECT ARRESTED 9 YEARS AFTER NORTH CAROLINA COLLEGE STUDENT FAITH HEDGEPETH KILLING They arrived back at the apartment at around 3:40 a.m. Rosario said she became sick from drinking before leaving at about 4:25 a.m. to stay with a friend. Rosario said Hedgepeth was conscious and breathing when she left. She later called Hedgepeth for a ride. Hedgepeth did not answer the call. Another friend, Marisol Rangel, drove Rosario home. They entered the apartment around 11 a.m. and found Hedgepeth beside her bed, Rosario said. Rosario described blood on the walls, the bed and Hedgepeth's arm. She told a 911 dispatcher that Hedgepeth felt cold to the touch. Rosario said she asked about an ambulance when police arrived. "I asked if they were still going to bring the ambulance, but they said she was gone," she testified. DNA testing Police collected DNA at the scene and tested hundreds of samples from people connected to Hedgepeth. None matched. DNA BREAKTHROUGH LEADS TO ARREST IN GRISLY 33-YEAR-OLD COLD CASE INVESTIGATORS NEVER GAVE UP ON Investigators eventually turned to genetic genealogy, a technique that compares crime-scene DNA with profiles in public ancestry databases. The information led to Salguero-Olivares, a stranger to Hedgepeth’s loved ones. Authorities received a break nearly a decade later. On Sept. 16, 2021, police pulled Salguero-Olivares over during a DUI stop in Wake County, N.C. After obtaining a DNA sample, they charged him with murder. Prosecutors later added the rape, sexual offense and burglary charges. The evidence On Friday, prosecutors presented items recovered from the bedroom, including a Bacardi rum bottle, a wine bottle and a crumpled Time-Out restaurant biscuit bag. Investigators found a profanity-laced handwritten message on the fast-food bag that read, "I'm not stupid, b----. Jealous." Chapel Hill police forensic technician Tamika Price displayed the 1.75-liter rum bottle to the court, which prosecutors identified as the murder weapon used to deliver blows to Hedgepeth’s head. "When I put my hands on her head, I could feel where the side of her head was very soft. It was indented," Price testified, ABC 11 reported. Questions about the investigation Under cross-examination, defense attorney James J. Rainsford pressed investigators on how they collected and preserved crime scene evidence. Price testified that an initial test indicated the stain could be blood, but investigators could not find the swab for further laboratory testing. articles.body: Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg joined a protest outside a high school in Paris on Tuesday, as French students took to the streets for another day of demonstrations over poor school conditions.Thunberg, who first rose to prominence as a teenager campaigning against climate change and has since expanded her activism to other causes, expressed support for the French students, saying they deserved “wider support.”“They should know that all over the world we are following these developments. articles.title: Super El Niño breaks sea temperature record weeks ahead of expected peak
articles.summary: El Niño has continued to strengthen, with several key measures now in record territory. Simon King explores how it compares to previous events.
articles.body:
El Niño has continued to strengthen to what some scientists are calling "unprecedented levels", weeks before its expected peak in December.

Several key measures are now in record territory.

It comes after scientists declared a new record for daily sea surface temperatures in the central-eastern Pacific in September, exceeding the previous record set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

Temperatures above 30C have also been recorded for the first time in parts of the tropical Pacific, while record sea-surface temperature anomalies and exceptional subsurface warmth have been observed.

These measurements come from the region of the equatorial Pacific used to monitor El Niño.

El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.

However, the Pacific is also warming due to human-induced climate change and this is starting to mask the strength of the natural warming during El Niño.

To remove this additional warming signal, Australian and US official forecasters are now using a Relative Ocean El Niño Index (RONI), to enable better comparison to historical events.

Using that measure, the BOM's average weekly data - while only going back to 2008 - is significant as it now exceeds levels during the record-breaking December of 2015 .

"We are currently witnessing an El Niño event that is unprecedented in the historical record," Dr Zeke Hausfather, a climate scientist at Berkeley Earth, told the BBC.

The warmth across the Pacific now extends well beyond the tropical region normally used to monitor El Niño.

Comparisons with previous major events in 1972-73, 1982-83, 1997-98 and 2015-16 show much more widespread ocean warmth across the Pacific and into the Gulf of Mexico.

Part of this reflects the long-term warming of the oceans but scientists say it is not the whole story.

"The strength of El Niño this year is spilling out of the traditional El Niño region," Dr Hausfather said.

Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

What is El Niño and why could it mean record temperatures?

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says there is currently no evidence that climate change is making El Niño events stronger or more frequent , external . However, it remains an active area of scientific research.

What is clearer is that El Niño releases additional heat from the oceans into the atmosphere.

Historically, global temperatures during El Niño years are typically higher than during neutral years.

Combined with human-driven climate change, that extra heat is expected to help make 2026 one of the warmest years on record, with unusually high global temperatures likely to continue into 2027.

Although the most widespread impacts are expected later this year and into 2027, El Niño's influence is already being felt across parts of the world.

The strength of an El Niño does not automatically determine the scale of impacts in any one location. Regional effects can vary considerably from one event to another.

However, some common patterns are emerging when compared with previous super El Niños.

During the 1997-98 event, severe drought across south-east Asia contributed to extensive peat and forest fires, while parts of East Africa experienced devastating floods.

The event also helped make 1998 the warmest year on record at the time.

A similar pattern developed during the 2015-16 El Niño.

Severe drought and wildfire activity returned to parts of south-east Asia, while southern Africa experienced one of its worst droughts in decades, triggering a major humanitarian crisis.

Another recurring signal is tropical cyclone activity. Strong El Niño events typically suppress Atlantic hurricanes while boosting activity across parts of the Pacific, a pattern that has also been observed during 2026.

The World Meteorological Organisation says drought and flood-related disruption is already being reported in several regions, with growing concerns over food security in parts of East Africa and the Asia-Pacific.

Forecasts from both the European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts and the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration indicate El Niño is likely to peak in December.

Dr Hausfather said the latest projections were "astonishing" and are likely to set new records "by a remarkable amount".

articles.title: Pembrokeshire mum told to prepare for 'worst' urges others to get respiratory illness vaccine
articles.summary: Jo Goldsmith said the RSV vaccine was not available when she was pregnant, but that she would have had it.
articles.body:
A woman whose newborn daughter became ill after catching a potentially serious respiratory illness is urging other pregnant women to make sure they are vaccinated against it.

Jo Goldsmith said she was told to "prepare for the worst" after her daughter Phoebe contracted respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) a few days after being born.

The vaccine was not available at the time of her pregnancy, but she said she "definitely would have had it".

"I wouldn't want any family to go through what we went through," she said.

Nerys Evans, Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health, is also urging people to make sure they are vaccinated against Covid-19, flu and RSV ahead of the winter months.

RSV is a common cause of coughs and colds, and although infections usually get better by themselves, they can sometimes be serious for babies and older adults, according to the NHS.

RHS vaccinations were introduced in Wales in September 2024.

Goldsmith, a children's nurse and health visitor from Haverfordwest, Pembrokeshire, said that when Phoebe was born four years ago, she realised within days that something was wrong.

"She was five days old, she had quite a lot of congestion… and we noticed quite quickly that she seemed to be breathing very fast and was struggling," she said.

She said she took Phoebe to hospital and "it escalated from there", with the family told on Christmas Eve that she had RSV positive bronchiolitis.

"So, we knew that we were going to be in [hospital] for the Christmas period. But we didn't quite realise how unwell she was going to be."

Phoebe soon deteriorated and was admitted to the hospital's high dependency unit, and Goldsmith said her experience as a nurse told her "we were going to be in for a bit of a rough ride".

But she said Phoebe took "her own unique path with it", and "really kept the doctors on their toes".

She said that after being taken to a room and shown an X-ray doctors "weren't quite sure which way we were going to go with things".

"They sort of prepared us for… the worse," she added.

Phoebe pulled through the virus but did face some longer-term problems, including being admitted to hospital several times with chest problems. Her hearing was also affected.

Goldsmith is now calling on others to be vaccinated against the illness, describing the experience as "the most traumatic thing we've had to go through".

"Watching your baby struggle to breathe and not knowing whether they were going to get through the next couple of hours, of what was going to happen overnight with them," she said.

What is RSV and who's eligible for the vaccine?

RSV is a common virus that circulates every winter. It usually causes mild symptoms, but for babies, older people and those with weakened immune systems, it can lead to serious illness, including bronchiolitis and pneumonia.

During a normal RSV season, infection in children under two years old is responsible for approximately 7,000 to 9,500 GP appointments and 2,300 to 2,600 hospital admissions in Wales.

It is estimated that RSV infection in over 75-year-olds is responsible for 7,000 to 9,000 GP appointments, 700 to 1,000 hospital admissions and 400 to 600 deaths in Wales each year.

The RSV vaccine is offered routinely year-round to all adults aged 75 and over, and pregnant women from 28 weeks – to help protect newborn babies from the virus. Older people only need the vaccine once and pregnant women should have the vaccine with every pregnancy.

The Welsh government is reminding people that the RSV vaccine is separate from the flu vaccine and should not be forgotten.

This autumn the offer of a RSV vaccine has also been extended to higher-risk adults aged 65 to 74, including those who are immunosuppressed or have chronic respiratory disease.

Evans, from the Welsh government, said Joanne's story was a "powerful reminder of how serious RSV can be", for older people and for babies.

"I urge all who are eligible to come forward for their flu jab, their COVID-19 booster and their RSV vaccine.

"They protect against different viruses, and it really can make the difference between a mild illness and a serious hospital stay," she said.

articles.title: Three things we've learnt about the UK economy from the IMF
articles.summary: The influential economics body has upgraded its UK growth forecast for this year, but risks remain.
articles.body:
Countries around the world have had their future economic prospects assessed by influential body, the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

What the IMF says matters – it aims to keep the global economy stable and its twice-yearly forecasts are one of the most authoritative looks at what is really going on around the world.

Yet like all forecasts they can also turn out to be incorrect, so they shouldn't be treated as gospel.

Here are three things we've learnt about the UK from the IMF's latest report.

1. The UK is weathering the Iran war better than expected

The global economy has been rocked by the US-Israel war with Iran.

The transportation and production of energy in the Middle East has been severely disrupted, causing oil prices to jump and inflation to rise.

To calm the rate of price rises, central banks, including the Bank of England, are expected to hike interest rates in the coming months.

Despite all this, the IMF said the global economy is doing much better than expected, partly because of the surge of investment into artificial intelligence (AI).

And this is good news for the UK. The IMF said its economy would expand by 1.3% in 2026, up from the 1% it predicted in July, before slowing in 2027.

A growing economy means companies are investing more and hiring more people while shoppers have more money to spend. A shrinking economy means the reverse is true.

2. The UK is doing better than other major economies

There is increased concern about how much money countries are borrowing, but the IMF said the UK is doing better than all other major economies at this.

The IMF said the UK "basically stands out, along with India" when it comes to addressing the problem and by 2031 it is projected to have the lowest annual borrowing of the G7 group of countries, which includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the US.

Sir Howard Davies, former deputy governor of the Bank of England, said this was largely because the UK has a government with a majority which has committed to tackling the situation, which it is expected to achieve either through tax rises, cuts to public services, or a mix of both.

By contrast, he says the US has said little about reducing its deficit, while France and Germany don't have majority governments.

"So, we [the UK] are not great students, but we look somewhat better than some of the others we are sharing the class with," he said.

Meanwhile, the IMF's growth forecasts for the UK mean it is expected to have the second-fastest growing economy in the G7 this year along with Germany.

Sir Howard believes this should also be seen in context.

"We're still growing slowly. It's almost like saying we're winning a slow bicycle race here because other people are going backwards a bit more rapidly than we are."

While the IMF boosted its projection for the UK's growth in 2026, it slightly downgraded its forecasts for next year.

While the UK has handled the economic fallout from the Iran war better than expected so far, it says this will change next year as high energy prices and elevated interest rates affect how much people spend in shops and how much companies are willing to invest.

In addition, the IMF has said households are likely to continue feeling the pinch of rising prices. It forecasts inflation in the UK will average 3.3% this year and it has raised its estimate for next year to 2.8% from its previous prediction of 2.4%.

"There will be increasing inflationary pressure put on the UK and the Bank of England will have to consider further rate rises," says Tim Armitage, investment strategist at Quilter Cheviot.

He added that at least one rate rise is predicted this year, with more expected to come next year.

articles.title: Drones could fly deliveries from France to Alderney
articles.summary: A firm in Paris has been working with Alderney Chamber of Commerce on a feasibility study.
articles.body:
A drone company is working with business leaders in the Channel Islands to explore the viability of drones for goods delivery on the island of Alderney.

Paris-based firm DragonFlyPads has been working with Alderney Chamber of Commerce to gather views on the idea, which could include "urgent deliveries" of items such as medical supplies.

The chamber said it had been approached by the company about using Alderney as a "platform" for deliveries, initially flying from Cherbourg.

Sissel Thorstensen, CEO of DragonFlyPads, said the project was in the "feasibility study stage" but businesses had shown "considerable interest".

Thorstensen said the company had developed software to make the delivers "autonomous".

She added: "It really enables the drone, the operator and the landing infrastructure as well as the traffic management - as well as even weather data - to all come together and communicate through one integrated system."

Meanwhile, the results of a survey canvassing islanders on "feasibility and potential demand for a small-package drone deliver service", were now being reviewed, the chamber said.

It said the goal was to explore whether "rapid, low-carbon aerial transit" could help local businesses overcome "transport bottlenecks" and speed emergency orders.

articles.title: Man killed in tiger attack identified as William Chapman
articles.summary: A health and safety investigation is under way at Yorkshire Wildlife Park following the incident.
articles.body:
The man who was killed by a tiger after entering its enclosure at a wildlife park has been identified as William Chapman, the BBC understands.

Chapman entered the enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park near Doncaster shortly after 13:30 BST on Saturday and was pronounced dead at the scene, according to South Yorkshire Police.

An eyewitness described seeing him wearing headphones and "pacing around" near the enclosure before he went in and was attacked. Police confirmed he was visiting the park on his own.

A force spokesperson said his family was aware and was being supported by specialist officers. The park was evacuated after the incident and remains closed as investigations continue.

City of Doncaster Council has also launched a health and safety investigation into the death, which a spokesperson said was "in line with our statutory duties".

Yorkshire Wildlife Park said their "thoughts and heartfelt sympathies" were with the man's family and confirmed the rare Amur tiger, called Altai, remained in the enclosure and would not be euthanised.

Chapman, described by eyewitnesses as in his 20s, was reported to have entered the enclosure after climbing down from a walkway.

Those who saw the attack said some witnesses had tried unsuccessfully to distract the tiger .

A video posted on a social media account believed to be Chapman's appears to show the moments before the attack.

In the footage, shot on a mobile phone, the inside of the enclosure can be seen as he approaches the tiger - perched on a wooden platform - across a patch of grass.

Shouts of concern, urging him to get out, can be heard.

The video ends, and the account has now been removed.

A spokesperson for the Born Free Foundation, which campaigns to phase out zoos, called for an "urgent review" into "how the man managed to enter the enclosure and what happened next".

Dr Campbell Murn, a previous member of the government's zoo expert committee and lecturer at the University of Reading, said while it was a tragic incident, determined people could get inside zoo enclosures.

"I view it in the same way a determined thief will get into somebody's house or somebody's car and despite the best security systems and enclosures sometimes these things happen," he said.

Ella Ford, 24, from Moreton, Wirral, had visited the park with her boyfriend and filmed the tiger moments before the attack.

She described seeing Chapman by the tiger enclosure "pacing around with his headphones in".

A few minutes later, she saw he had "climbed up onto the barriers".

A woman was close by talking to him, she said, before "he jumped in and crawled in front of the tiger, where the tiger was perched and just lay there".

Ford said she then witnessed the tiger grab hold of him, and he was "shouting for help".

She estimates around 15 to 20 people were on the enclosure's raised visitor walkway before staff quickly evacuated the area, and shortly afterwards, the park.

She described members of the public as being "confused, like what on earth's going on?"

"I just know some man was obviously trying to bang on the fence to try and deter the tiger away, but it obviously wasn't doing anything," she said.

Karmelle Pelham, 39, from Worksop, had been enjoying a family day out when park staff told them the site was being evacuated.

She said she had heard what sounded like "gunshots" and an air ambulance had circled above.

Pelham added: "There was a big, black tarpaulin over the tiger enclosure."

She praised park staff for their handling of the incident, saying it had been "very, very well organised".

articles.title: Creeslough: Planning permission for petrol station overturned
articles.summary: Ten people died in the blast at a petrol station in Creeslough, County Donegal, on 7 October 2022.
articles.body:
A decision to grant planning permission for a new petrol station near the site of a deadly explosion in Creeslough, County Donegal, four years ago has been overturned.

The blast, which killed 10 people , happened at a service station in the County Donegal village on 7 October 2022.

In March, Donegal County Council approved a planning application permitting the construction of a new service station in the village, close to the site of the blast.

On Tuesday, An Coimisiún Pleanála (the Republic of Ireland's planning commission) refused permission following an appeal by some relatives of those killed in the explosion.

The planning commission said a significant portion of the land earmarked for the planned development was zoned as an "amenity area".

That means it is designated for "open space purposes and to make provision for new recreation, leisure and community facilities".

As such, a commercial development on the site, the commission said, would go against the site's designation.

It would also be "contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area" and would "establish an undesirable precedent for future similar developments on amenity zoned lands", the commission said.

Speaking to BBC News NI in March, when the plan was granted permission by Donegal County Council, Áine Flanagan, whose partner Robert Garwe and daughter Shauna Flanagan-Garwe were killed, said the decision to approve the plans was "morally and ethically wrong".

It is the second time a proposal for a new petrol station in the village has been overturned by An Coimisiún Pleanála.

Planning permission for a new development on the actual site of the blast was granted last year but was later overturned following an appeal by the bereaved families.

The most recent application would have seen a new building constructed to include a shop, post office and deli.

The plans also detailed a forecourt, underground fuel storage tanks and pumps, a car wash, outdoor launderette kiosk and an ATM.

The 10 victims of the explosion included four men, three women, two teenagers and a five-year-old girl - all from the village or surrounding areas.

Those who died were Robert Garwe and his five-year-old daughter Shauna Flanagan-Garwe; Catherine O'Donnell and her 13-year-old son James Monaghan; Jessica Gallagher; Martin McGill; James O'Flaherty; Martina Martin; Hugh Kelly; and 14-year-old Leona Harper.

No official explanation has yet been given for the cause of the explosion.

A primary investigation file was forwarded to the Republic's Director of Public Prosecutions last September by Gardaí (Irish police).

Earlier this year Irish police sent a second file to prosecutors that includes "formal recommendations".

articles.title: RJ Mitte: How Breaking Bad star changed the way we see cerebral palsy
articles.summary: The star, who has died at the age of 34, fought for better representation of disabilities on screen.
articles.body:
"I have cerebral palsy but I've never let it hold me back."

Those are the words of a 22-year-old Breaking Bad star RJ Mitte in an essay for Huffpost back in 2014.

Explaining his experiences of learning to stand up to bullies while growing up, he added: "It shouldn't define you. I just happen to have CP."

That was also true of Mitte's character Walter 'Flynn' White Jr, the son of Bryan Cranston's character in the drama, which was recently named the best TV show of the 21st Century by the New York Times.

"What I really like is that he was on TV playing a character that had cerebral palsy, but it wasn't about the fact that he had cerebral palsy," says Emma Livingstone, founder and CEO of Up - the Adult Cerebral Palsy Movement.

"When we see RJ Mitte on TV just playing a role, but who also happens to have CP, I think that's really powerful."

Mitte, who died by suicide on Monday at the age of 34 , wasn't just an actor - he was also an advocate and supporter, working as an ambassador for charities including United Cerebral Palsy and Can Do Canines, as well as creating The Mitte Foundation, which offered community grants in his home town in Texas.

Susan Sellers, president and CEO of United Cerebral Palsy, says: "His advocacy was rooted in a commitment to ensuring that people with cerebral palsy and other disabilities are seen, heard, and afforded the opportunity to reach their full potential."

Mitte's legacy, particularly for performers with disabilities, is significant.

Ruth Madeley, who stars as disability rights advocate Judy Heumann in new film Being Heumann, tells the BBC: "If you don't see it, you don't think it's possible. When I was younger, acting wasn't even on my radar. I didn't even think it was an option."

The actress, who has spina bifida, adds: "To have people like him [Mitte] on screen for so many young people looking at the arts as an industry that they want to get into... He was just a beautiful example of that.

"But he wasn't just a disabled person breaking down barriers in the industry. He was a phenomenal talent, and I think that's what's going to be missed so much."

Another actor, Keron Day, who appeared in Netflix hit Sex Education, tells the BBC: "My biggest tribute I can pay to RJ and his work is that I am emailing you today from a set of a TV show.

"That is his legacy: disabled people having careers within the creative industries. If I could have half the impact that RJ has had, I would be enormously proud. It's a sad day for both our industry and our community."

Comedian and screenwriter Laurence Clarke concurs. "The more portrayals that we see on TV, that's going to inspire more disabled people to think it's a career for them," he says.

"Things have moved on a long way since Breaking Bad came out in 2008. But there's always further to go."

Speaking of Mitte's role in Breaking Bad, Clarke tells the BBC: "What's beautiful about it is that the disability is visibly there, always."

He also notes the impact on people watching inclusive dramas and shows.

"The more you're exposed to those portrayals, as members of the public, it becomes just part of life, and how you see the world."

Mitte was aged three when he was diagnosed with cerebral palsy, which the NHS describes as the name for a group of lifelong conditions that affect movement and co-ordination caused by a problem with the brain that develops around birth.

He was cast in Breaking Bad at 14, and told Channel 4 News in 2016 that the show "pioneered a lot of TV and writers to be more brave".

But he added a note of caution, saying: "We still have a long way to go... it's still a business and we have to do that slowly."

Earlier this month, he hinted that he may be interested in continuing the Breaking Bad story , but said any revival would have a lot to live up to.

"I just want to top Breaking Bad, that's the hardest," he said. "I set a bar for myself as a young man that is kinda unattainable. I tell people, 'Look, it's a long way down from the top of the mountain'."

After Breaking Bad, Mitte's other on-screen credits include Hannah Montana, Switched at Birth, Westhampton and his latest project, Talking to Strangers, which came out earlier this year.

But his biggest achievement - and his greatest pride - was his philanthropic work.

"Where I felt most top of the world was being able to help others through Breaking Bad, with the work I've done with people with disabilities... trying to remind people they have a voice and [to] lend my voice.

"The greatest thing that Breaking Bad has given me is to be able to lend my voice to causes that make a meaningful impact, that change people's lives."

articles.title: Trump administration asks Don Jr's ex-girlfriend Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as US ambassador to Greece amid cash-for-access allegations
articles.summary: President Donald Trump has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as US ambassador to Greece, White House new press secretary Katie Zacharia announced in her
articles.body: President Donald Trump has asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign as US ambassador to Greece, White House new press secretary Katie Zacharia announced in her first press conference today. This came amid several allegations of abuse of power against Guilfoyle who was engaged to Donald Trump Jr for years."She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well," Zacharia said.The allegations, reported exclusively by The Wall Street Journal, concern both Guilfoyle's conduct before her confirmation as ambassador and her tenure in Athens. Her lawyers have denied wrongdoing, saying a disputed payment request related to unpaid fees for earlier public appearances and speaking engagements rather than her diplomatic position.$100,000 credit card bill and alleged promise of accessOne of the most serious allegations concerns businessman Eric Deters, a Trump supporter and donor who said Guilfoyle asked him to pay a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing in July 2025.According to messages provided by Deters to news organizations, Guilfoyle allegedly urged him to transfer the money directly to the credit card company. One message reportedly said that the payment would not show up anywhere if sent directly to American Express.Deters alleged that Guilfoyle offered to help him gain access to senior officials in the Trump administration in return for the payment. He described the arrangement as a quid pro quo. He told NBC News that she had indicated he could ask her for virtually anything within the Trump administration.The messages were reportedly exchanged shortly before her July 9, 2025, confirmation hearing. Deters said he did not pay the money.Guilfoyle's lawyers disputed the allegations, arguing that the money concerned fees for speaking engagements and public appearances that predated her nomination. The controversy prompted the State Department's Office of Inspector General to investigate Guilfoyle and the US embassy in Greece, according to NBC News.Alleged threat involving the Greek governmentA separate report by The Wall Street Journal alleged that Guilfoyle told guests at a reception that the United States could undermine the Greek government if it chose to do so.The report also raised questions about her interactions with Greek business interests. She was accused of promoting the interests of a particular Greek construction and energy company and allowing its lobbyist to attend private diplomatic meetings.These allegations have raised concerns about whether private commercial interests were being given inappropriate access to diplomatic channels. The reported accounts have not, by themselves, established that Guilfoyle violated any law or diplomatic rule.Luxury travel and gifts from business interestsGuilfoyle has also faced questions over alleged gifts, services and luxury travel involving business figures. A Wall Street Journal report described her frustration at being excluded from a Greek-themed event organised during the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, earlier this year.According to the reporting, Guilfoyle demanded to attend the event and spoke about luxury trips to France with energy company executives. The broader allegations have raised questions about whether benefits provided by private business interests were appropriate for a serving US ambassador.Separately, reports have described tensions between Guilfoyle and staff at the US embassy in Athens over her leadership and conduct. The State Department watchdog's investigation is examining concerns involving Guilfoyle and the embassy, although the department has not publicly confirmed the details of the inquiry.Who is Kimberly Guilfoyle?The controversy has put the administration in a tough spot as she has not only been an envoy but also a part of the Trump family for years. articles.title: Massive bison rams pickup truck in Yellowstone after driver tries to avoid collision
articles.summary: A bull bison charged a man's Ford Ranger near Mud Volcano in Yellowstone National Park around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday — and fortunately, the man did not report injuries.
articles.body: A driver's early-morning trip through Yellowstone National Park took a frightening turn when a bison suddenly charged his pickup truck. A video shared on Facebook shows the massive animal standing on a dark roadway before rushing toward the vehicle — then slamming into the front of the truck. The driver had stopped his Ford Ranger after spotting the bull bison near Mud Volcano at around 2:45 a.m. on Thursday, according to Wyoming publication Cowboy State Daily. Rather than attempting to pass, he hit the brakes and waited for the bison to move. "I slammed on my brakes and stopped, and was just sitting there watching and waiting for him to continue walking," Weber told Cowboy State Daily. After he waited, the animal remained on the roadway — and then unexpectedly charged the pickup and hit its front-left side, according to the outlet. The collision dented the truck's bumper and hood, and it broke a side marker light, according to Cowboy State Daily. articles.title: Claude Lalanne’s bronze armchair with monkeys, vines, and an ostrich-leather seat sold for $1.079 million after reaching Sotheby’s through its online consignment portal
articles.summary: A unique gilt-bronze armchair by French designer Claude Lalanne sold for $1,079,500 in December 2025 after arriving through the auction house’s
articles.body: A unique gilt-bronze armchair by French designer Claude Lalanne sold for $1,079,500 in December 2025 after arriving through the auction house’s consignment portal. The chair features a frame wrapped in vines and monkeys cast in patinated bronze, paired with a seat made from ostrich leather.According to Sotheby’s, the armchair was made in 1998 and numbered one from an edition of one. The piece reached Sotheby’s through its consignment portal before selling for $1,079,500 in December 2025. The armchair was sold at a time when demand for Lalanne’s works was particularly strong. The same Sotheby’s auction was led by another piece that set a record for the highest price paid for a design object at auction.How did Sotheby’s sell Claude Lalanne’s armchair for $1.079 millionThe gilt-bronze armchair by Claude Lalanne sold for $1,079,500 at Sotheby’s in December 2025. Its distinctive design combines a chair frame wrapped in vines and monkeys cast in patinated bronze with a seat made from ostrich leather. The piece reached the auction house through its consignment portal, showing how an online submission can lead to the sale of a significant design object.Margaret Wood, a specialist in Sotheby’s Design Department, described the chair as the earliest of Lalanne’s ‘Singerie’ armchairs to appear at auction. Its sale placed the unique design among the notable works to emerge through Sotheby’s consignment process.What makes Lalanne’s Singerie armchair different from other designsThe armchair’s design centres on its bronze vines and monkeys, which wrap around the underlying chair form. articles.title: Running on empty, Trump turns to Putin to fuel midterm hopes
articles.summary: The TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump insists Russia and China are not doing much to help Iran in its war with America and
articles.body: The TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump insists Russia and China are not doing much to help Iran in its war with America and Israel. “If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all,” the MAGA supremo declared on Monday, arguing that Moscow and Beijing had too much to lose by getting involved.The assessment is not universally shared by American pundits who have pointed to Russian intelligence assistance to Tehran and Chinese-linked supplies of technology and components that could sustain Iran’s military capabilities. Yet Trump appears determined not to let such doubts obstruct his relationship with either leader, ties now on display with his puzzling call to buy Russian diesel and his decision to attend an APEC meeting in Shenzhen in November where he will meet Xi for a second time in two months, to likely be followed by a third in December at the G-20 meet in Florida.In a move that has infuriated Ukraine, unsettled European allies, mystified India, and prompted bipartisan protests in Washington, Trump has agreed to open the American market to Russian fuel -- in itself remarkable for someone who brags incessantly about the U.S being energy surplus -- while easing sanctions imposed to punish Moscow for invading Ukraine. The ostensible reason is soaring diesel prices ahead of midterm elections on Nov 3, with Trump needing to show that he can bring down the cost of living to forestall a rout.The electoral calculation is straightforward: Diesel is the lifeblood of trucking, agriculture, construction and much of the goods-distribution economy and high prices raise operating costs for farmers and truckers, feeding into consumer prices to provide Democrats with an obvious line of attack against a president who promised manna. Small problem: the transaction is so insignificant -- the initial shipment would cover less than a day's demand in the U.S and the first three announced tranches would amount to only a few days' consumption -- that analysts are looking for hidden agenda in the deal.While Russia stands to earn hundreds of millions of dollars from the initial shipments, the broader waiver provides Moscow with an opportunity to resume exports and challenge the principle that its energy revenues should be restricted while its war against Ukraine continues -- the argument Washington made while bearing down on India.Trump, predictably, has doubled down on the two-timing. On Monday he invoked the European Union's past purchases of Russian energy, claiming the bloc had paid Russia $250 billion, without specifying the period covered. His argument is essentially that Washington should not be held to a stricter standard than European capitals, hypocrisy from both sides (U.S and Europe) that New Delhi called out from the get-go.Trump's reluctance to stand up to -- much less confront – Putin and Xi is not necessarily evidence of personal affinity alone, according to diplomatic observers; it reflects a transactional view of diplomacy in which personal relationships with powerful leaders are treated as instruments of statecraft, and immediate economic or political gains can outweigh the longer-term costs of accommodating strategic rivals.Amid renewed jokes about Russian asset and Moscow's puppet, some experts have said the deal with Putin is “purely diplomatic” -- arguing that it was designed to put Ukrainian President Zelenskyy in a corner -- while others insist its main motivation is domestic In either case, the deal reinforces a familiar criticism of Trump: the appearance of a personal triumph over the painstaking construction of an effective strategy. Whether voters reward him will depend on what they see at the gas pump -- and if they believe the president has delivered results rather than another announcement. At present, the diesel deal looks less like a solution to Trump's midterm gambit than a small shipment carrying an outsized geopolitical cost.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Trinamool leader Baiswanor Chattopadhyay questioned again by Kolkata police over Camac Street hoarding clash; FIRs also name Abhishek Banerjee, Derek O’Brien.
articles.body: Kolkata: Senior Trinamool functionary and former mayor-in-council member Baiswanor Chattopadhyay appeared before Shakespeare Sarani police on Tuesday for a fresh round of questioning in connection with an alleged clash during the removal of an unauthorised party hoarding.This was Chattopadhyay’s second appearance after he was first summoned on Sept 3. articles.title: Amit Shah in Kol on Sat on 2-day visit, to visit Belur Math, puja pandals
articles.summary: Amit Shah to visit Belur Math and four Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata-Howrah on Oct 17-18 (Saptami); stays at Soujanya, departs for Delhi Oct 18.
articles.body: Kolkata: Union home minister Amit Shah is scheduled to visit Belur Math and four Durga Puja pandals in Kolkata and its outskirts during his two-day visit to Bengal on Oct 17 and 18 – the two days of Saptami.According to the tour plan released by the ministry of home affairs, Shah is scheduled to land at Kolkata airport from Ahmedabad around 8 pm on Saturday and will stay at Soujanya, the state govt guest house in Alipore.On Sunday, he will spend around 30 minutes at Belur Math and visit the Durga Puja pandal of Bali Deshbandhu Club in Howrah.The home minister will then have lunch at Soujanya and is then likely to visit the Chetla 24 Palli and Sreebhumi Sporting Club pandals and Shobhabazar Rajbari. Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari is likely to accompany Shah during his pandal visits.Shah is scheduled to depart for Delhi from Kolkata airport around 3.05pm.The state govt had extended invitations to both PM Narendra Modi and Shah to attend the grand Mahalaya programme at Eden Gardens. articles.title: Sweet-making units found flouting norms
articles.summary: Bihar food safety raids in Patna seized and destroyed contaminated sweets, paneer and expired ingredients; licences cancelled or suspended ahead of festivals.
articles.body: Patna: The state food safety department seized and destroyed 170kg of foul-smelling sweets and paneer at a Kankarbagh confectionery on Tuesday and confiscated milk cake and ‘peda’ worth Rs 5 lakh from another outlet during festive-season inspections. Officials also found fungal growth in food items and serious hygiene violations at several establishments.The action followed the cancellation of manufacturing licences of two sweet-making units and suspension of another unit’s licence in Patna on Monday over food safety violations.The health department has been inspecting restaurants, hotels and food manufacturing units across Bihar for over a month with checks focusing on sweetshops in recent days. The drive, ordered by secretary-cum-food safety commissioner Kumar Ravi, aims to prevent the sale of adulterated, expired and contaminated food during Durga Puja and Diwali.At a confectionery in Hanuman Nagar, Kankarbagh, officials destroyed 120kg of chhena sweets, 20kg of jaggery sweets, 10kg of mixed sweets and 20kg of paneer. The chhena sweets and paneer were valued at Rs 41,000. Another Kankarbagh outlet was found storing 3,344kg of milk cake and 112kg of peda, which were seized. A confectionery near Kadamkuan had a bathroom in its kitchen area.On Monday, two units in Buddha Colony lost their manufacturing licences after expired ingredients were found. One stored expired gram flour, refined flour and wheat flour worth Rs 18,335, while 70kg of expired gram flour was destroyed. Expired custard powder, flavouring material and baking powder were found and destroyed at the second unit. Another unit’s licence was suspended, with its operator given three days to explain the violations.At a Ramkrishna Nagar sweet shop, officials destroyed 630kg of kalakand, 10kg of barfi and 5kg of laddoo worth Rs 1 lakh. In Indira Nagar, spoiled milk powder and other food items were seized and destroyed.Recent inspections also revealed poor sanitation, damaged floors and walls, inadequate lighting, improper storage and missing pest-control arrangements and water-testing reports. articles.title: Headmaster arrested for sexual abuse of Class VI student
articles.summary: Headmaster of Mayurbhanj ashram school arrested after Class VI student alleges sexual abuse; case filed under BNS and POCSO, probe continues.
articles.body: Balasore: A headmaster of an ashram school in Mayurbhanj district was arrested on Tuesday following allegations of sexual abuse by a Class VI student.The accused headmaster had reportedly gone absconding after a complaint was filed. Following a search operation, he was detained at his residence late on Monday night, Rairangpur superintendent of police Suresh Patra said, adding that further investigation into the case is underway.According to police, the alleged incident took place on Sept 25. The accused allegedly called the Class VI girl to his office on the pretext of closing doors and windows. The minor later alleged that she was sexually abused inside the office.Sources said the student initially informed two hostel matrons about the incident. However, it is alleged that efforts were made to suppress the matter. The incident came to light after the student informed her parents about it over phone on Monday.Acting on a written complaint lodged by the girl's father, police launched an investigation.
